title: Token Unit Econ Pilot: Latency-Aware Batching + Cache + Quantization Framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a focused pilot that bundles latency-aware batching, proactive KV prefix caching, and targeted int8/int4 quantization configurations into a repeatable framework. Goal: empirically validate ~15% unit token cost reduction across representative workloads while preserving P95 latency and output quality. Deliver a gated rollout playbook and a dashboard for per-route economics and quality regressions. This ticket tracks roadmap, success metrics, rollout criteria, and required engineering/obs tasks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pilot runs on three customer-representative workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings) for at least 2 weeks each. 2) Measured unit cost reduction >= 12% overall and >=8% for chat workloads. 3) P95 latency increase <= 12% vs baseline and absolute P95 <= 120ms for interactive routes. 4) No quality regression on held-out eval prompt sets (auto-detected regressions <= 1.5% on BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics). 5) Rollout playbook and one-click console preset created and reviewed by Eng and DX teams.
milestones: Define workload matrix and success thresholds - 2026-02-25
Implement pilot bundling config & API flag - 2026-03-05
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quantization introduces subtle quality regressions on long-context summarization. Mitigation: Add per-prompt eval filters and fallback rules to route >4k token contexts to full-precision model variants. Risk: Batching increases tail latency for low-QPS routes. Mitigation: Latency-aware batching threshold with real-time SLO detector and emergency bypass flag.
